units.title: Hello & Introductions
units.intro: Greet people, say who you are, and ask people to slow down.
culture: Family name first
Chinese names put the family name first, just like Vietnamese names. In 林小玉, the family name is 林 (Lín).
不好意思 is everywhere
Taiwanese people say 不好意思 to get attention, to pass someone, or to soften a request. It is polite, not a big apology.
"Have you eaten?"
Older people may greet you with 你吃飽了嗎？ ("Have you eaten?"). It just means hello. Answer 吃飽了 ("I have") with a smile.
Teachers
Call teachers 老師 (lǎoshī), even outside class: 林老師, 王老師.

phrases.hv: Vietnamese cảm ơn comes from 感恩 (gǎn'ēn), "to feel grateful."

phrases.note: Used all the time: to get someone's attention, to squeeze past, or for a small apology.
A real apology. For small things, 不好意思 is more natural.
Start any question to a stranger with 請問.

phrases.hv: Ngọc is 玉 (yù, jade) in Chinese, so 小玉 is a friendly Chinese nickname for Ngoc.

phrases.en: I study at Ming Chuan University.
I can speak a little Chinese.
Please speak a little more slowly.

cast.B: 阿玲 (a new student from Vietnam)

lines.en: Hi! Are you a new classmate?
Yes, my name is A-Ling.
Where are you from?
I'm from Vietnam.
Your Chinese is very good!

lines.zh: 謝謝！我會說一點中文。請說慢一點。
lines.en: Thanks! I can speak a little Chinese. Please speak more slowly.

lines.zh: 好！我叫阿明。很高興認識你。
lines.en: Sure! I'm A-Ming. Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you, too.

quiz.q: What does A-Ling ask A-Ming to do?

units.title: Numbers, Money & Time
units.intro: Count, talk about prices, and ask about the time and the day.
culture: Two kinds of "two"
Count with 二 (èr): 一、二、三. But before a measure word use 兩 (liǎng): 兩個人 (two people), 兩杯茶 (two cups of tea).
Lucky and unlucky numbers
8 (bā) sounds like 發 ("to prosper"), so people love it in phone numbers. 4 (sì) sounds like 死 ("death"), so some buildings and hospitals skip the 4th floor.
Dates go from big to small
Taiwan writes the year, then the month, then the day: 2026年11月10日. Official papers often use the Republic of China (民國) year: 2026 is 民國115年.
Taiwan money
Coins are NT$1, 5, 10, and 50. Bills are NT$100, 500, and 1,000 (NT$200 and 2,000 bills exist but are rare). Prices are written with 元 and spoken with 塊.

phrases.note: Before a measure word, say 兩 (liǎng), not 二: 兩個, 兩杯, 兩張.
Prices are written with 元 (yuán). In everyday speech people also say 塊 (kuài).

phrases.en: Can you make it a little cheaper?
phrases.note: You can ask at some markets, but not in stores or convenience stores.
In Taiwan 期 is read qí (rising tone).

signs.en: Second item at 60% of the price

lines.en: Are you free tomorrow?
Yes, I'm free in the afternoon.
Shall we go see a movie?
Sure! What time?
Two thirty. Let's meet at the MRT station.
How much are the movie tickets?
280 dollars each.
OK, see you tomorrow!

quiz.q: When are they going to the movie?

units.title: Convenience Store
units.intro: Pay, heat up food, use your EasyCard, and answer the questions clerks always ask.
culture: More than a store
At 7-Eleven (people call it 小七, Xiǎo Qī, "Little Seven") and FamilyMart (全家, Quánjiā) you can pay bills, print documents, buy train tickets, and pick up online orders.
Every receipt is a lottery ticket
Taiwan's receipts (發票, fāpiào) have a lottery number. Prizes are drawn every two months, on the 25th of odd-numbered months. Keep your receipts!
The e-receipt barcode
A 載具 saves your receipts on your phone, so you don't lose the lottery numbers. You can set one up in the Ministry of Finance e-invoice app.
The EasyCard
The 悠遊卡 (yōuyóukǎ) works on the MRT, buses, YouBike, and in most convenience stores. You can add money at the store counter.
units.hv: 便利 = tiện lợi, so 便利商店 is literally a "tiện lợi" store.

phrases.note: Clerks say this every time the door opens. You don't need to answer.
Plastic bags are not free in Taiwan, so clerks always ask.

phrases.en: Do you have an e-receipt barcode?
phrases.note: A 載具 is a barcode on your phone that saves your receipts. If you don't have one, just say 沒有 (méiyǒu).

phrases.en: Do you want it heated up?

phrases.note: 麻煩你 ("sorry to trouble you") is a polite way to say yes, please.

phrases.en: Can I pay by credit card?
Excuse me, do you sell umbrellas?

lines.en: Welcome!

lines.zh: 你好，這個便當可以加熱嗎？
lines.en: Hi, can you heat up this lunch box?
Sure. Do you need a bag?

lines.zh: 不用，謝謝。可以用悠遊卡嗎？
lines.en: No, thanks. Can I use my EasyCard?

lines.zh: 可以。一共八十九元。有載具嗎？
lines.en: Yes. That's 89 dollars. Do you have an e-receipt barcode?
No, I don't.
OK, thanks for coming!

quiz.q: Does the customer take a bag?

units.title: Night Markets & Bubble Tea
units.intro: Order street food, say no to spicy or cilantro, and order bubble tea just the way you like it.
culture: Choose your sweetness
Drink shops ask 甜度 (sweetness): 全糖 full, 少糖 less, 半糖 half, 微糖 a little, 無糖 none. And 冰塊 (ice): 正常冰 regular, 少冰 less, 微冰 a little, 去冰 none, 熱 hot.
Night markets
At night market stalls you usually order and pay first, and many take cash only. Carry some NT$100 bills and coins.
Vegetarian food
Vegetarian (素食, sùshí) restaurants are easy to find. Look for the character 素 on the sign.
A taste of home
Look for 越南河粉 (Yuènán héfěn, Vietnamese pho). Many Taiwanese people love it, and Vietnamese restaurants are in many neighborhoods.
No tipping
Tipping is not expected in Taiwan. Some sit-down restaurants add a 10% service charge to the bill.

phrases.en: Excuse me (boss), I'd like this one.
phrases.note: Call any food vendor 老闆 ("boss"). It is friendly and normal.

phrases.hv: 珍珠 = trân châu and 茶 = trà, just like trà sữa trân châu.

phrases.en: How sweet, and how much ice?

phrases.note: In Taiwan 微 is read wéi (rising tone).

phrases.en: Can I pay now? / The check, please.

lines.en: Hi, what would you like to drink?
I'd like a bubble tea.
Large or medium?
Large.
How sweet, and how much ice?
Half sugar, less ice.
For here or to go?
To go, thanks.
OK, that's 65 dollars.

quiz.q: What size does the customer order?

units.title: Getting Around
units.intro: Ride the MRT, buses, and taxis, and ask for directions.
culture: No food or drink on the MRT
Inside the MRT gates you can't eat, drink, or chew gum, not even water. The fine is NT$1,500 to NT$7,500.
Priority seats
The dark blue seats are 博愛座, for older people, pregnant women, and people who need them. Many Taiwanese leave them empty even on a crowded train.
Escalators
Many people in Taipei stand on the right so others can walk on the left. The MRT asks everyone to hold the handrail, so follow what people around you do.
Buses
Wave at the bus to make it stop. Tap your EasyCard when you get on, and on some buses when you get off too. The sign 上車收費 or 下車收費 tells you when to pay.
YouBike
The yellow YouBike bicycles are everywhere in Taipei. Register your EasyCard in the YouBike app, then tap it on the dock to ride.

phrases.en: Excuse me, how do I get to Taipei Main Station?
Turn left at the traffic light.
Does this bus go to Shilin?
How long does it take to walk?
Please take me to this address.
phrases.note: In a taxi, show the address on your phone and say this.
Say this to get past people on a crowded train or sidewalk.

lines.zh: 不好意思，請問捷運站在哪裡？
lines.en: Excuse me, where is the MRT station?

lines.zh: 往前直走，在紅綠燈右轉。
lines.en: Go straight ahead and turn right at the traffic light.
How long is the walk?
About five minutes.
I'm going to Tamsui. Do I need to transfer?
No, the Red Line goes all the way there.
Great, thank you!
You're welcome!

quiz.q: Where should the student turn right?
Does the student need to transfer?
quiz.a: No, the Red Line goes there
wrong: The student has to take a bus

units.title: Campus Life
units.intro: Talk with teachers and classmates, find your way around campus, and make friends.
culture: LINE is everything
Classes, clubs, and teachers use LINE groups for announcements and homework. If you're not in the class group, ask the class representative (班代, bāndài) to add you.
Join a club
At the start of each semester there is a club fair. Joining a club (社團) is the fastest way to make Taiwanese friends.
Teachers' Day
September 28 is Teachers' Day in Taiwan, the birthday of Confucius. Students often give teachers a card or a small gift.
Asking for help
Taiwanese students may be shy about speaking English, but most are happy to help. Ask in Chinese first, even a little. People really appreciate it.

phrases.en: How do you say this character?

phrases.note: 禮拜 and 星期 both mean "week." 禮拜 is more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: What time does the library close?
Can I add you on LINE?
I'm taking the day off today.
phrases.note: 請假 means asking for leave from class or work. Tell your teacher before class if you can.

phrases.en: You can do it! / Go for it!
phrases.note: Literally "add oil." Say it before a test, a game, or anything hard.

lines.en: Did you understand what the teacher said?

lines.zh: 一半而已。作業什麼時候交？
lines.en: Only half. When is the homework due?

lines.zh: 下禮拜三。我們一起去圖書館寫吧。
lines.en: Next Wednesday. Let's go to the library and do it together.
Sure! What time does the library close?
Ten at night.
Then let's have dinner first.
OK. Can I add you on LINE?
Of course!

quiz.q: How much of the class did A-Ling understand?
What time does the library close?

units.title: Health & Emergencies
units.intro: See a doctor, buy medicine, and get help in an emergency.
culture: Emergency numbers
119 is for an ambulance or fire. 110 is for the police. Both work from any phone, even without a SIM card.
Health insurance

After six months in Taiwan, international students join the National Health Insurance (健保, jiànbǎo) and get a card. Until then, your school's student insurance covers you. Ask your university's international office.
Clinics first
For a cold or a small injury, go to a neighborhood clinic (診所, zhěnsuǒ). It's quick and cheap. Big hospitals are for serious problems.
Masks
If you have a cold, wearing a mask in class or on the MRT is polite. Nobody will think it's strange.
Earthquakes
Taiwan has many small earthquakes. If the shaking is strong: drop, cover, and hold on under a table, and stay away from windows.

phrases.en: I have a cough and a sore throat.
phrases.note: In Taiwan 咳 is read ké (rising tone).

phrases.en: I'd like to register to see a doctor.
phrases.note: At a clinic, first register (掛號) at the counter with your health insurance card or passport.

phrases.en: Here is my health insurance card.
How many times a day do I take it?

phrases.hv: 過敏 = quá mẫn (the medical word for an allergy).

lines.en: Hello, what's wrong?
I have a fever, and my throat really hurts.
When did it start?
Last night.
Are you allergic to any medicine?
No.

lines.zh: 好，這個藥一天吃三次，飯後吃。多喝水，多休息。
lines.en: OK. Take this medicine three times a day, after meals. Drink lots of water and get plenty of rest.
OK, thank you, doctor.

quiz.a: A fever and a sore throat

quiz.q: Is the patient allergic to any medicine?
How should the patient take the medicine?
quiz.a: Three times a day, after meals

units.title: Home & Errands
units.intro: Take out the trash, fix things at home, mail packages, and run errands.
culture: Chasing the garbage truck
Most streets have no trash cans. Instead, garbage trucks come at set times and play music, often Beethoven's "Für Elise." People wait outside and throw their bags in.
Sorting trash
Separate general trash, recycling, and food scraps (廚餘). In Taipei and New Taipei, general trash must go in official city trash bags, sold at convenience stores.
The post office
Chunghwa Post (中華郵政) is also a bank. Many international students open a postal savings account there. Bring your passport and your residence card (ARC).
Shoes off
Take off your shoes when you enter a Taiwanese home. Your host will usually give you slippers.

phrases.en: What time does the garbage truck come?
phrases.note: In Taiwan 垃圾 is read lèsè.

phrases.en: Where do I put food scraps?
How do I use the washing machine?
Can you fix it for me?
I'd like to send a package to Vietnam.
I'd like to open an account.
I'd like to get a phone number.

phrases.zh: 不好意思，可以小聲一點嗎？
phrases.en: Excuse me, could you be a little quieter?

lines.zh: 房東先生，不好意思，熱水器壞了。
lines.en: Excuse me, sir, the water heater is broken.
There's no hot water?

lines.zh: 對，從昨天開始就沒有了。
lines.en: Right. There's been none since yesterday.

lines.zh: 好，我明天早上找人去修。
lines.en: OK, I'll get someone to fix it tomorrow morning.

lines.zh: 謝謝。還有，垃圾車幾點來？
lines.en: Thanks. Also, what time does the garbage truck come?

lines.zh: 晚上七點半。聽到音樂就要出去倒。
lines.en: 7:30 in the evening. When you hear the music, take your trash out.
OK, got it.

quiz.q: When does the garbage truck come?
How do you know the garbage truck is coming?

units.title: Customs & Festivals
units.intro: Festival greetings, gift rules, and the everyday manners Taiwanese people notice.
culture: Gifts to avoid
Don't give a clock: 送鐘 ("give a clock") sounds like 送終 ("see someone off at death"). Umbrellas (傘, sǎn) sound like 散 ("to break apart"). Avoid giving things in fours.
Red and white
Red envelopes are for happy times: New Year, weddings, birthdays. White envelopes are for funerals. Put money in red envelopes in even amounts, but never with a 4.
Chopsticks
Never stand chopsticks up in a bowl of rice. It looks like the incense sticks offered to the dead.
The festival year

Lunar New Year (January or February), the Lantern Festival, Tomb-Sweeping Day (early April), the Dragon Boat Festival, and the Mid-Autumn Festival, when many Taiwanese families have a barbecue outside.
Ghost Month
The seventh lunar month (usually August) is Ghost Month. Many Taiwanese avoid swimming, moving house, or whistling at night. You don't have to believe it, but it's polite to know.

phrases.note: The classic Lunar New Year greeting.
phrases.hv: 恭喜發財 = cung hỷ phát tài, the same greeting Vietnamese people use at Tết.
中秋 = Trung Thu, as in Tết Trung Thu.

phrases.en: I wish you all the best.
This is a small gift for you.
phrases.note: Say this when you give a gift. Give and receive gifts with both hands.
Hosts and servers say this when they serve food.

phrases.en: Should I take off my shoes?
You're welcome to visit my home.
Thanks for all your hard work!
phrases.note: Say it to anyone who has worked hard for you: a teacher, a driver, a classmate after a project.

phrases.en: To pray at a temple (also: bye-bye!)
phrases.note: 拜拜 means both "bye-bye" and worshipping at a temple. You'll hear both every day.

lines.zh: 新年快樂！歡迎你來我家過年。
lines.en: Happy New Year! Welcome to my home for the New Year.

lines.zh: 新年快樂！這是一點小心意。
lines.en: Happy New Year! This is a small gift for you.
Pineapple cakes! You're too kind.
Should I take off my shoes?
Yes, here are some slippers.
Vietnam celebrates Lunar New Year too.

lines.zh: 真的嗎？你們也發紅包嗎？
lines.en: Really? Do you give red envelopes too?
Yes, we give red envelopes too.

quiz.a: Take them off and wear slippers

quiz.q: What does A-Ling say about Vietnam?
quiz.a: It celebrates Lunar New Year too
wrong: It has no New Year holiday

units.title: Places to Visit
units.intro: Plan trips, buy tickets, and explore Taipei, the north coast, and beyond.
culture: Taipei favorites
Taipei 101, the National Palace Museum (故宮), Shilin Night Market, the sunset at Tamsui (淡水), and the hot springs and hiking trails of Yangmingshan (陽明山).
Day trips from Taipei
Jiufen's old street on the mountainside, the sky lanterns at Shifen (十分), and the strange rock shapes at Yehliu (野柳) on the north coast.
Come to Changhua
Lukang (鹿港) has old streets and temples hundreds of years old. In Changhua City, see the Great Buddha on Baguashan (八卦山) and try Changhua's famous meatball dumplings (肉圓, bah-uân).
Farther away
Sun Moon Lake (日月潭), the sunrise at Alishan (阿里山), Tainan (台南), the old capital full of great food, and Taroko Gorge (太魯閣) in Hualien. Check which trails are open before you go.
Getting there
The High Speed Rail (高鐵) runs down the west coast: Taipei to Changhua takes about an hour. It has discounts for college students on some trains.

phrases.en: I'd like to go to Jiufen.
How much is the admission ticket?
Could you take a photo of us?
What time is the last train (or bus)?
How do I get to Yangmingshan?
I'd like to go up Taipei 101 to see the city at night.
Do you want to go to Lukang together?

phrases.zh: 鹿港在彰化，有很多老廟。
phrases.en: Lukang is in Changhua. It has many old temples.

lines.en: Are you free this weekend?
Yes! Where do you want to go?
How about Jiufen?

lines.zh: 好啊！聽說那裡的芋圓很有名。
lines.en: Sure! I heard the taro balls there are famous.

lines.zh: 對，而且晚上的風景好漂亮。
lines.en: Yes, and the view at night is beautiful.
How do we get there?

lines.zh: 坐火車到瑞芳，再坐公車上山。
lines.en: Take the train to Ruifang, then a bus up the mountain.

lines.zh: 週末人很多，我們早一點出發吧。
lines.en: It's crowded on weekends, so let's leave a little early.

quiz.a: Train to Ruifang, then a bus

units.title: Classroom Chinese
units.intro: Simple Chinese for helping at a Taiwanese school: instructions, praise, and classroom routines.
culture: Children with Vietnamese moms
Many Taiwanese children have mothers from Vietnam. Vietnamese is one of the "new resident languages" (新住民語文) that elementary schools can teach. Your lesson can make these children proud.
Who's who at school
Call the principal 校長 (xiàozhǎng) and a director 主任 (zhǔrèn), often with the family name: 王主任. Every teacher is 老師.
Lunch nap
After lunch, students put their heads down on their desks for a nap (午休, wǔxiū), usually until about 1:20. Keep quiet in the hallways then.
Cleaning time
Taiwanese students clean their own classrooms and school grounds every day (打掃時間). There are no janitors in most classrooms.

lines.en: Welcome to our school!

lines.zh: 謝謝主任！我今天要介紹越南文化。
lines.en: Thank you, Director! Today I'll introduce Vietnamese culture.

lines.zh: 太好了。三年級的小朋友在等你。
lines.en: Great. The third graders are waiting for you.
How many students are in a class?

lines.zh: 二十五個。有幾個小朋友的媽媽是越南人。
lines.en: Twenty-five. A few of the children have Vietnamese mothers.

lines.zh: 真的嗎？那我教他們說越南話！
lines.en: Really? Then I'll teach them some Vietnamese!

lines.zh: 他們一定很高興。投影機在這裡。
lines.en: They'll be so happy. The projector is over here.
OK, thank you!

quiz.q: What will the visiting teacher do today?
How many students are in the class?
What is special about some of the children?
